bug_semantics: Optional PKCE in handleAuthorizationCodeGrant can be skipped by a downgrade: parseAuthRequest stores code_challenge only if the authorization request includes it, and the token endpoint verifies a code_verifier only when the grant already has codeChallenge (isPkceEnabled = !!grantData.codeChallenge). RFC 9700 §2.1.1/§4.8.2 requires rejecting a token request that carries code_verifier unless a code_challenge was present at authorization. Without that mismatch check, an attacker who strips code_challenge from the authorization request causes the AS to persist a non-PKCE grant; a later token request is then accepted without PKCE, completely bypassing the intended code-binding defense (CWE-287). GHSA/CNA: npm @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider < 0.0.5, patched in 0.0.5.
flaw_origin: First public write of PKCE is b1079e7beb5f4821a0ffc7ae07670c417b66d07d ('Ask Claude to implement PKCE support (for OAuth 2.1).'). That commit added oauth-provider.ts parseAuthRequest optional code_challenge capture (lines 1226-1236), grant persistence of those fields (1275-1277), and handleAuthorizationCodeGrant's skip-if-absent verifier (722-752: if (grantData.codeChallenge) { ... } with no else-if rejecting a verifier when no challenge was stored). Immediate parent 4fb0f128cce4306bde33c14b2309833be669c826 has no PKCE symbols. 7d3fdde29c540c67867e653311cb635203cab627 only refactored the same predicate to isPkceEnabled = !!grantData.codeChallenge; 941684c4398a5da9bcbfb9550b0ee0c5213db796 moved the file to src/oauth-provider.ts. The RFC 9700 mismatch reject was not written until d954473f066f0daa3949717fd4d6e805d2ac618b.

reasoning: CVE-2025-4144 / GHSA-qgp8-v765-qxx9 is a published CNA advisory for a PKCE downgrade in workers-oauth-provider, not a withdrawn/false-positive record. The mechanism is the RFC 9700 skip: PKCE is enforced only when a grant already stores codeChallenge, so stripping code_challenge at authorize leaves a grant that accepts a token request without (or ignoring) PKCE. The smallest first-write of that optional-store plus skip-if-absent verifier is b1079e7beb5f4821a0ffc7ae07670c417b66d07d; its parent tree has zero PKCE identifiers, so introducer_parent_absent remains false. Later 7d3fdde is a predicate rename (grantData.codeChallenge -> isPkceEnabled) and 941684c is a path move; neither first wrote the hole. The fix is the mismatch reject in d954473, merged to main as 09a2adb and released as npm 0.0.5 immediately afterward; BIC is an ancestor of affected v0.0.4 and the fix is not. AI is judged only on that BIC commit object: author/committer are Kenton Varda, there are no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with trailers, but the commit message itself is an explicit Claude Code authorship/prompt record for the PKCE implementation that first wrote the flawed check. That is commit-object AI authorship of the introducing change, so the verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE rather than NOT_AI or AI_CODE_FLAWED.
